title: Know We
label: Solid City (per Reynolds; FACT says self-released)
format: Dubplate from late 1999, then vinyl (white labels sold to shops by Wiley, per RBMA)

type.basis: Produced by Wiley. Simon Reynolds lists it in his Grime Primer for The Wire (dated 2005 on one reposting, 2013 on another); FACT (2013) calls it vanguard grime. Its string hook and MC-first space anticipate Wiley's later records.

sound.text: Reynolds (Wire 'Grime Primer', 2005, reposted 2015): simple programmed beats and a single violin-flourish hook, with the MCs carrying the track.
Trench (2019): ominous string riffs and harder-hitting drum sequences, like 'a rap cypher in a rave'.
FACT (2013): gritty and gruff, with a skeletal rhythm and bass drone and the MC as the focus.
Mixmag (2018): 'clearly demarcated space for MCs to fill with complex rhymes'.

context.text: A dubplate circulated from late 1999 before the official 2000 release; the crew grew out of shows on the pirate station Rinse FM (Wikipedia).
Reynolds (Wire Grime Primer, 2005, reposted 2015) says it circulated on dubplate as early as 1999 and was in constant pirate rotation by its release.
Crew members included Wiley, Maxwell D, Flowdan, God's Gift, Slimzee, DJ Target, Geeneus, Breeze, Plague, Bubbles and Major Ace; remnants later formed Roll Deep.
In Mixmag (2018) Dan Hancox reports that Geeneus claims it as the first ever grime track; Hancox himself calls it a paradigm shift towards tracks built around MCs.
RBMA (Emma Warren, 2015): Maxwell D says the tune 'started a buzz'; the article says it cemented the Pay As U Go and Bow crews, and that Wiley sold copies direct to record shops.

calls.label: UK garage (crew-level infobox), credited with paving the way for grime
garage rap, in a list headed Grime Primer
grime: claimed as the first grime track

rels.other: Roll Deep Entourage – Terrible (Reynolds calls them a chip-off-the-same-block pair; shops treated Terrible as its follow-up)
Pay As U Go – Champagne Dance (2002)

uncertainty: Year conflicts: 2000 (Wikipedia, FACT, Mixmag) vs 2001 (Reynolds). Label conflicts: Solid City (Reynolds), self-released (FACT), later Teebone (RBMA). No catalogue number found because Discogs was unavailable. Reynolds's 2001 'Unfaves of 2000' text reposted in the same post describes the 2001 pirate garage-rap sound generally, so it was not assigned to this record specifically.
tracklist: Debut single of the crew. Per RBMA, Wiley later licensed it to Teebone in a bundle with 'Terrible' and 'Wickedest Ting'.
